## Santa Cruz Highlands: Where to See Giant Tortoises in the Wild

The interior of [Santa Cruz Island](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/) in the Galápagos is strikingly different from its coastal areas. Dry lava fields gradually give way to greener, more humid grasslands and patches of forest. Giant land tortoises roam freely here, slowly grazing and resting in the shade.

The highlands attract travelers with the chance to **see giant tortoises in their natural habitat**, not only in a breeding center or conservation facility. You can watch the animals' ordinary behavior: selecting grass, moving around and interacting. There is no need to approach them closely to appreciate the experience.

## Where Are the Highlands and How Do You Get There?

Santa Cruz is one of the main visitor islands of the [Galápagos Archipelago](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). Many travelers fly into [Baltra](/ecuador/place/baltra-island/), cross the channel and travel by road through the island toward [Puerto Ayora](/ecuador/place/puerto-ayora/). The road crosses different natural zones and makes a stop in the highlands possible along the way.

This is not a single museum with one entrance, but a broad region containing several sites where organized walks and tortoise observation are possible. Access rules, admission fees and time needed depend on the site chosen and current conditions.

On some itineraries, the highland visit takes place during part of the arrival day. Allow extra time for a more detailed introduction to the vegetation and volcanic landscape.

## Why Tortoises Live Among the Humid Vegetation

Galápagos land tortoises use different natural zones of the island depending on season and food availability. The green highlands provide grass and other plants, and migrating tortoises can sometimes be seen in different areas.

The number of tortoises near the paths varies. Sightings of dozens cannot be guaranteed on every date. Watching wildlife is rewarding precisely because the animals behave naturally rather than according to a prearranged schedule.

The Galápagos National Park runs monitoring and conservation programs for giant tortoises. Its staff return rehabilitated animals to their natural Santa Cruz habitats and work to restore populations across the archipelago.

## How to Observe a Giant Tortoise

A large domed shell, massive legs and a long neck make these animals easy to recognize. Watch quietly and you will see that a tortoise does not stay still all the time: it selects food, walks slowly among plants and sometimes changes direction when somebody blocks its path.

The best way to photograph a tortoise is to remain in a permitted spot at a distance and wait. Do not attract its attention, knock on the shell or stand immediately in front of its face. According to national park rules, **the minimum distance from wildlife is two meters**, even if the animal approaches on its own.

Do not touch, feed or lift tortoises, or put children on them for a photograph. Such actions harm the animals and break the protected-area rules.

## Highland Forest and Volcanic Landscapes

The humid interior of Santa Cruz has different vegetation and a different microclimate from the dry shores. Pastures, shrubs and native forest communities grow here. Some places contain Scalesia trees, creating an unusual forest environment for oceanic islands.

Some Santa Cruz excursions combine tortoise watching with lava tunnels. These form when the outer surface of a flowing stream of lava hardens while molten material keeps moving inside. Once the inner lava drains away, a hollow tube remains.

However, a lava tunnel is a separate attraction. A program mentioning only the highlands and tortoises does not automatically include an underground visit.

## Highlands Versus a Tortoise Breeding Center

| Experience | Main purpose |
|---|---|
| Highlands | Observing animals in the wild |
| Breeding center | Protecting tortoise populations |
| Lava tunnel | Island geology |
| Marine outing | Marine wildlife |

Breeding centers help specialists raise young tortoises and return them to their natural habitat. The highlands let you observe animals where they live independently. Marine excursions feature other Galápagos wildlife, including sea lions, rays and sea turtles.

These experiences complement one another but take place in different locations and sometimes require separate excursions.

## When to Plan Your Visit

The highlands receive more moisture than some coastal parts of the island. During rainy periods, paths can be slippery and vegetation grows denser. Weather and the locations of tortoises vary in other months.

Comfortable closed shoes, light rain protection, sunscreen and water are useful for walking. Soil can be soft after rain. Stay on official paths and follow your guide's advice.

When choosing dates, consider your overall [Ecuador itinerary](/ecuador/) and seasonal conditions at the particular site, rather than assuming one universally ideal day for tortoise watching.

## Santa Cruz Highlands in Ada Tours Programs

On the [Galápagos Diving: Four or Five Days tour](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-diving-4-5-days/), we include a guided highlands visit on the arrival day. After landing at Baltra, guests see the tortoises and have lunch, then continue to the Fiesta Hotel and prepare for later dives.

This land-based part of the itinerary introduces animals that live on shore before the marine excursions begin. Subsequent days focus on scuba diving. The exact dive sites and number of dives depend on which version of the tour you choose.

The highlands also feature in the geography of a [12-day Ecuador and Colombia journey](/multi-country/tour/ecuador-colombia-galapagos-12-days/). You can also compare [nature and wildlife tours](/interests/wildlife/) and [diving journeys](/interests/diving/). In every case, distinguish the main route from separate optional activities.

## Frequently Asked Questions About the Santa Cruz Highlands

### Can You See Giant Tortoises Living Freely?

Yes. They live and roam in their natural environment in designated highland areas open to visitors. Their exact numbers and locations change.

### Is This the Same Place as the Tortoise Breeding Center?

No. A breeding-center visit introduces population recovery work. The highlands are for observing free-ranging tortoises.

### Can You Visit the Highlands on the Way from the Airport?

Yes. Some programs include this after arriving on [Baltra](/ecuador/place/baltra-island/), on the way to [Puerto Ayora](/ecuador/place/puerto-ayora/). Check the itinerary to confirm the particular stop.

### Can You Feed or Pet the Tortoises?

No. The national park prohibits feeding and touching wild animals. Keep at least two meters away.

## Which Tours Visit the Santa Cruz Highlands?

The [Santa Cruz Highlands](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-highlands/) lie in the elevated interior of [Santa Cruz Island](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/) in the Galápagos. This area is greener and wetter than the dry shoreline. Among open grasslands and forest vegetation, you may see giant land tortoises and native land birds.

Our collection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} that feature the highlands as part of their main geography. But **listing the region on a route does not determine the length of an excursion or its included services**. One program explicitly features tortoises and a guide, while others include the highlands within a multi-day island section.

## Which Program Should You Choose?

| Travel format | Role of the highlands |
|---|---|
| Four- or five-day diving trip | Guided tortoise visit on arrival |
| Twelve-day Ecuador and Colombia | Highlands on the Santa Cruz route |
| Thirty-two days through eight countries | One stop on a large island itinerary |

On the [Galápagos Diving: Four or Five Days tour](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-diving-4-5-days/), travelers land on [Baltra](/ecuador/place/baltra-island/), visit the highlands to see tortoises with a guide, have lunch and then become acquainted with the dive center and equipment. This is followed by two or three diving days, depending on the chosen version. It suits people whose main goal is scuba diving, complemented by a land-based wildlife experience.

On the [12-day Ecuador and Colombia tour](/multi-country/tour/ecuador-colombia-galapagos-12-days/), the highlands form part of the arrival day on Santa Cruz and the transfer toward [Puerto Ayora](/ecuador/place/puerto-ayora/). The journey continues with marine excursions and Colombian cities. If you want extended tortoise watching, check that day's exact schedule: a place list alone does not indicate how long the stop lasts.

The [32-day tour of eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) also includes Santa Cruz and the highlands during its island section. It suits people seeking broad geographic coverage, so there is less time for a long visit to one particular site than on a dedicated Galápagos holiday.

## Why Travelers Come to See Giant Tortoises

Large land tortoises are among the archipelago's distinctive animals. In the highlands they can move across open ground and feed on plants. You can watch them without specialized marine equipment, seeing their slow movements, the shape of their shells and the habitat itself.

Wild animals do not follow a timetable. Tortoises wander freely, and observations depend on the location and time. Follow your guide's instructions, keep your distance and do not feed, touch or corner an animal to get a photograph.

In addition to the tortoises, the highlands show a different side of Galápagos vegetation. Instead of lava-covered shores, boats and sea lions, there are humid green slopes and forest patches. Even on a short tour this adds depth to your understanding of the island.

## Connecting Baltra, the Highlands and Puerto Ayora

Many visitors fly into the airport on [Baltra Island](/ecuador/place/baltra-island/), cross the Itabaca Channel and drive across Santa Cruz toward [Puerto Ayora](/ecuador/place/puerto-ayora/). Along the way, natural conditions shift from the drier northern part of the island to the greenery of the interior.

That makes a highland stop convenient on a transfer day. Visitors can see land animals before marine excursions begin, without an additional long journey. However, the duration depends on arrival time, hotel location and other scheduled activities.

Some tours combine the highlands with [Los Gemelos Twin Craters](/ecuador/place/los-gemelos/), volcanic depressions in the forest. These are a separate attraction. **Mentioning the highlands does not automatically include Los Gemelos**; check for them in the particular program.

## What to Bring and How to Plan Your Day

The island's interior can be cooler and wetter than the coast. Wear closed shoes with non-slip soles, a light rain jacket and comfortable walking clothes. The ground may be slippery after rainfall.

If your itinerary combines highlands and diving, distinguish the requirements. Watching tortoises on land needs no underwater training. Marine outings depend on participants' experience, ocean conditions and the guides' decisions. Compare formats in [diving tours](/interests/diving/tours/) and [Ecuador wildlife tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/ecuador/).

## Frequently Asked Questions About Tours Through the Santa Cruz Highlands

### Which Tour Explicitly Includes a Guided Tortoise Visit?

The [four- or five-day diving tour](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-diving-4-5-days/) includes a highland tortoise visit with a guide and lunch on its first day. A sighting of a particular animal at a particular time cannot be guaranteed.

### Are the Highlands and Santa Cruz Island the Same Place?

The highlands are a natural region of [Santa Cruz Island](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/). The island also includes a coast, port and settlements. A tour may visit Santa Cruz without offering a long separate excursion through the highlands.

### Can I Combine a Highland Visit with Arrival at Baltra?

Yes. Some programs stop here between Baltra Airport and the Santa Cruz hotel. The order depends on flight time and the day's planned services.

### Do I Need Diving Experience to Walk Among the Tortoises?

No. This is a land-based nature visit that requires no diving skills. Diving experience matters only for the marine section of the specialized journey.

## Santa Cruz Island in the Galápagos: Tortoises, Volcanoes and Marine Routes

Santa Cruz is one of the main islands of Ecuador's [Galápagos Archipelago](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). On a single land trip, you can experience dry coastal areas, green highlands and the southern shore with [Puerto Ayora](/ecuador/place/puerto-ayora/). It works both as a nature destination in its own right and as a base for boat outings.

What distinguishes Santa Cruz from some smaller volcanic islands is the chance to **see giant land tortoises in their natural environment** without needing a marine cruise. Other days may be spent exploring lava tunnels, visiting nearby islands or walking around town. The excursion mix depends on the actual program.

## Highlands: Giant Tortoises and Lava Tunnels

The island's interior is more humid and green than its northern shore. Giant land tortoises and Darwin's finches inhabit the [Santa Cruz Highlands](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-highlands/). Visitors observe them from land as tortoises feed, rest in the grass and move between patches of vegetation.

Some itineraries include a private nature reserve or farm where these animals can be observed. The particular site, guiding and admission arrangements depend on the tour. Touching, feeding or chasing a tortoise for photographs is prohibited.

Lava tunnels are another reminder of the Galápagos' volcanic origins. They formed when the outer surface of a lava flow cooled before its interior; underground cavities remained after the lava stopped flowing. Only tunnels officially open to visitors may be entered. Closed shoes and extra lighting may be useful depending on the site.

## North, Highlands and South: How They Differ

| Part of the island | Main feature |
|---|---|
| North | Itabaca Channel and dry shore |
| Highlands | Tortoises and lava tunnels |
| South | Puerto Ayora, harbor and hotels |

Even clothing choices depend on this distinction. Open areas are sunnier and windier, while the highlands can be cooler and more humid. For a drive across the island, bring water, a hat and light rain or wind protection.

Do not confuse Santa Cruz with [Baltra Island](/ecuador/place/baltra-island/). Baltra has the airport used by many flights from mainland [Ecuador](/ecuador/). The two islands are separated by the Itabaca Channel.

## Getting from Baltra to Puerto Ayora

After landing on Baltra, visitors take ground transport to the Itabaca crossing. On the other side, Santa Cruz begins, and the road then runs across the island to [Puerto Ayora](/ecuador/place/puerto-ayora/) on the southern coast. In other words, landing at the airport does not mean you have already reached your hotel.

On our [Complete Ecuador for New Year: Andes and Galápagos tour](/ecuador/tour/complete-ecuador-new-year/), the arrival day includes traveling across the highlands, observing giant tortoises and visiting lava tunnels. The group then reaches its hotel in Puerto Ayora. This is an example of making good use of an arrival day for land excursions. Other itineraries may schedule the highlands on a different day.

Special conservation and transport procedures apply when entering the archipelago. Check current documents, fees and luggage inspections before travel: they are not the same as routine check-in for a domestic flight.

## Where to Go by Sea from Santa Cruz

Santa Cruz often serves as a land-based accommodation hub, with travelers returning to their hotels after day trips at sea. But **not every boat departs from Puerto Ayora harbor**. Depending on the program, you may first need a road transfer to the north of the island before boarding a boat.

[Bartolomé Island](/ecuador/place/bartolome-island/) is known for its panorama of Pinnacle Rock, volcanic slopes and marine snorkeling areas. Other trips lead to North Seymour, South Plaza or Bachas Beach. They differ in birdlife, habitats and landing arrangements; the generic term "Galápagos excursion" tells you too little to compare them.

On the [New Year tour](/ecuador/tour/complete-ecuador-new-year/), Bartolomé has its own full day, while the following sea excursion has **one of two options**: North Seymour and Bachas Beach, or South Plaza and Cape Carrión. These are alternatives, not all simultaneously included. When choosing, consider the number of actual island days, excursion options and which stops are confirmed after booking.

## How Many Days to Spend on Santa Cruz?

If tortoises, lava tunnels and the main landscapes are your priority, begin with one dedicated land-excursion day. A boat trip to Bartolomé requires another full day. A walk around Puerto Ayora fits well into an evening after returning.

Count **full days between flights**, rather than only the total nights in the Galápagos. Boat journeys take time for transfers, embarkation and the return crossing; poor weather can change schedules. Adding too many islands to a short journey reduces the time available to enjoy the very experiences you came for.

## Wildlife Observation Rules

Galápagos National Park requires visitors to keep at least two meters from animals, prohibits touching and feeding them, and requires people to stay on authorized trails. Do not collect plants, sand, shells or stones. These rules help protect an island environment where many species evolved under relatively limited human influence.

For a wider range of islands and programs, browse the [Ecuador tour catalog](/ecuador/tour/) and the [Galápagos guide](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/).

## Frequently Asked Questions About Santa Cruz Island

### Can I See Giant Tortoises Without Going on a Cruise?

Yes. A land excursion to the [Santa Cruz Highlands](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-highlands/) allows you to observe land tortoises. The particular site and visiting conditions depend on the tour.

### Are Santa Cruz and Puerto Ayora the Same Place?

No. Santa Cruz is a large island with several natural zones, while [Puerto Ayora](/ecuador/place/puerto-ayora/) is a town on its southern coast. Reaching the highlands requires another journey inland.

### Can I Visit Bartolomé and Return to My Hotel on the Same Day?

Yes. For example, this format appears on an [Ada Tours itinerary](/ecuador/tour/complete-ecuador-new-year/). Departure times, landings and sea activities depend on the boat schedule and marine conditions.

## How to Choose a Tour Including Santa Cruz Island

[Santa Cruz Island](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/) is part of the Galápagos Archipelago. [Puerto Ayora](/ecuador/place/puerto-ayora/) lies on its southern coast, and the [highlands with giant tortoises](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-highlands/) are inland. Many flights arrive via neighboring [Baltra](/ecuador/place/baltra-island/), after which visitors cross the Itabaca Channel.

Our catalog contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} featuring Santa Cruz on the main route. Yet **the same island plays different roles**. You may stay in a hotel and go diving, visit during a yacht cruise or spend a short stage here between flights on a much longer journey.

## Diving, Yacht Cruise or Multi-Region Tour?

| Format | Key feature |
|---|---|
| Hotel-based diving | Sea outings and returns to shore |
| Yacht cruise | Island crossings and landings |
| Ecuador with Galápagos | Mainland and island nature combined |
| Multi-country tour | Galápagos as one part of a longer route |

On the [four- or five-day diving program based at Hotel Fiesta](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-diving-4-5-days/), travelers use Santa Cruz as their land base. On the arrival day they visit tortoises in the highlands, followed by two or three diving days, each with two dives. Specific sites depend on sea conditions and the participants' experience. This works best for people who primarily want to dive rather than change islands every day.

On the [eight-day VIP Galápagos yacht cruise](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-luxury-yacht-cruise-8-days/), Santa Cruz forms part of the yacht itinerary alongside other islands. Nights, travel and landings are organized differently. The cruise explores several parts of the archipelago, but each visit follows the vessel's route and conservation regulations.

The [18-day Ecuador tour with a Galápagos wildlife cruise](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/) begins in the Andes and Amazon before continuing to the islands. Its cruise stage connects San Cristóbal, Floreana, Española and Santa Cruz. Compared with a short island-based program, it offers more ecosystems but also more extensive travel logistics.

On the [12-day Ecuador and Colombia journey](/multi-country/tour/ecuador-colombia-galapagos-12-days/), the island stage shares the itinerary with Quito, Medellín, Cartagena and Bogotá. The [32-day tour across eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) has an even wider reach. Choose these for their full multi-country combination, not with the expectation of a separate full week on Santa Cruz.

## What Happens on Arrival Day?

The airport on [Baltra](/ecuador/place/baltra-island/) is separate from Santa Cruz Island. After landing, travelers reach the Itabaca Channel, cross to Santa Cruz and drive inland. Some programs proceed directly to [Puerto Ayora](/ecuador/place/puerto-ayora/) and the hotel, while others include nature stops.

As you travel south, the scenery changes from dry terrain to greener interior areas. In the [Santa Cruz Highlands](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-highlands/), giant tortoises may be observed. The short diving tour explicitly includes this guided visit. The mere presence of Santa Cruz in another tour's name or list of places does not guarantee the same excursion day.

You should also distinguish [Los Gemelos Twin Craters](/ecuador/place/los-gemelos/) from the highlands generally. The craters are a separate volcanic attraction; check the exact itinerary to confirm a visit.

## Land Activities and What to Leave for the Marine Stage

Santa Cruz offers several sides of Galápagos life. [Puerto Ayora](/ecuador/place/puerto-ayora/) is a port town with urban amenities. The [Charles Darwin Research Station](/ecuador/place/charles-darwin-research-station/) introduces the archipelago's conservation and scientific work. The [highlands](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-highlands/) feature different vegetation and land tortoises.

But those three places do not automatically form one mandatory excursion. If a tour includes Santa Cruz, check the precise stops in its program and arrange any free-time activities or additions separately.

Marine experiences differ too. Diving involves several descents on selected days with a return to base. Cruises include inter-island crossings, shore landings or outings in smaller boats, depending on the approved itinerary. To visit other islands such as [Isabela](/ecuador/place/isabela-island/), choose a route that actually includes them rather than assuming a day trip from Puerto Ayora is available.

## Estimating Time and Preparing for the Journey

For a short island trip, the number of useful days on Santa Cruz and at sea matters more than the total travel duration. Combined tours spend some time on mainland flights and transfers; cruises use time for crossings between islands. Check where each night is spent and how many full days remain for your preferred activity.

Weather and ocean conditions affect marine excursions. On land, bring sun protection, closed shoes for nature walks and light rainwear. Diving requires consideration of the participant's experience and the conditions of selected sites; yacht travel requires an ability to tolerate sea crossings.

Pay particular attention to the journey back via Baltra and connecting flights. The island route includes both road and water transfers, and airport procedures take time. Do not plan tight international connections as though departing the Galápagos were a simple city transfer.

Compare [Ecuador tours](/ecuador/tour/), [wildlife trips](/interests/wildlife/tours/ecuador/), [diving tours](/interests/diving/tours/) and [cruises and expeditions](/interests/cruises-and-expeditions/tours/). They serve different purposes and help filter out programs that do not match your main interest.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Tours Including Santa Cruz Island

### Can I Explore Santa Cruz Without a Cruise?

Yes. The [four- or five-day diving program](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-diving-4-5-days/) uses hotel accommodation, with boat outings on separate days. No cruise yacht is required.

### Do All Island Tours Include Giant Tortoises?

No. Check the day-by-day details. The short diving tour explicitly includes a visit to the [tortoise highlands](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-highlands/), but other programs may spend less time on the island.

### How Is Santa Cruz Different from Baltra?

[Baltra](/ecuador/place/baltra-island/) has the arrival airport; [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/) is the neighboring island with Puerto Ayora, highlands and departure points for marine excursions. A crossing is required between them.

### How Do I Choose Between an Island Tour and Ecuador with Galápagos?

For a particular marine activity, a specialized tour may be best. To combine the islands with the Andes and Amazon, compare [combined Ecuador tours](/ecuador/tour/) and the number of days actually allocated to the archipelago.

## Santa Fe Island: Iguanas on Land and Sea Lions Underwater

[Santa Fe Island](/ecuador/place/santa-fe-island/) lies southeast of [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/) in Ecuador's Galápagos Archipelago. This small uninhabited island has coastal coves, prickly pear cacti and well-known sea lion colonies.

Santa Fe is particularly interesting because **different activities reveal different aspects of its wildlife**. On land, visitors may see a rare endemic land iguana on an authorized trail. Underwater, sea lions, reef fish, turtles and rays become the main attraction. A day trip by sea does not always include a landing, and a landing does not imply scuba diving.

## What Makes the Island's Wildlife Special?

Santa Fe has its own endemic land iguana, *Conolophus pallidus*, which occurs nowhere else. Its pale coloring and head shape distinguish it from more widespread Galápagos land iguanas. Prickly pear cactus is an important food source; large tree-like specimens grow on the island.

Santa Fe is also notable for its ecosystem restoration history after introduced goats were eliminated. Conservation projects monitor native animals and work to restore giant tortoises. This helps explain why visitor trails, landings and contact with wildlife are so strictly regulated.

An authorized land route begins at Barrington Bay on the northeast side. Sea lions rest on the shore, and paths lead through cactus groves and areas inhabited by land iguanas. Disembarkation is permitted only in accordance with national park rules and the approved excursion itinerary.

## Diving at Santa Fe: What Might You See?

The marine sites off the north and east shores include El Fondeador, La Encañada and Costa Este. Sea lions are a characteristic presence and may swim close to divers. Reef fish, sea turtles, rays and sometimes sharks also appear, depending on the site and conditions.

Our diving program lists **two possible dive sites** at Santa Fe. Moray eels, turtles, sea lions, reef fish, rays and bottom-dwelling invertebrates are described for these sites. The program gives an approximate boat transfer of one hour from base, though actual travel time depends on the departure point and sea conditions.

Do not expect the same set of animals at every site. Visibility, currents and waves change. Sea lions may be especially easy to observe on one visit, while on another the focus may be on small fish and animals among rocks. Close encounters should occur on the animals' terms, without chasing or attempting to touch them.

## Walking, Snorkeling and Diving: Which to Choose?

| Format | Main interest |
|---|---|
| Land walk | Cacti, iguanas and shore-dwelling sea lions |
| Snorkeling | Life near the surface in an authorized area |
| Scuba diving | Underwater slopes, fish, turtles and rays |

To see the land iguana, you need a permitted shore excursion. Scuba diving requires a boat, a suitable underwater site, equipment and eligibility to participate. Combining both formats in one day is possible only with **a specific confirmed itinerary** including both visits.

If you are more interested in large pelagic animals and stronger currents, compare Santa Fe with [Gordon Rocks](/ecuador/place/gordon-rocks/). For a volcanic reef with rock ledges and smaller marine life, consider [Cousins Rock](/ecuador/place/cousins-rock/). Choose according to skills and ocean conditions rather than an abstract dive-site ranking.

## Planning a Visit to Santa Fe

On [Ada Tours' Galápagos Diving program](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-diving-4-5-days/), we use a base on Santa Cruz. Four- and five-day options offer two or three diving days, respectively; two dives are planned on each diving day. Santa Fe is among the **possible**, not mandatory, sites. Selection depends on the dive center's schedule, weather, participants' qualifications and authorized routes.

The program specifies a recognized diving certification and a preliminary equipment check. If Santa Fe is your principal travel goal, state your preferred format before booking — walking, snorkeling or scuba diving — and confirm the actual route. "A trip to Santa Fe" alone does not convey which experiences are included.

National park rules require authorized boats and guides, staying on permitted trails and keeping a safe distance from animals. Photograph iguanas and sea lions without moving closer to get the shot or disturbing their ordinary behavior.

For other nature destinations, see [South Plaza Island](/ecuador/place/south-plaza-island/) for land trails and [Floreana Island](/ecuador/place/floreana-island/) for different coastal history and marine routes. Current scuba journeys are grouped under [Diving](/interests/diving/), while land-wildlife observation appears under [Nature and Wildlife](/interests/wildlife/).

## Frequently Asked Questions About Santa Fe Island

### How Is Santa Fe Different from Other Galápagos Islands?

Santa Fe is the only natural home of the land iguana *Conolophus pallidus*. It also has marine sites associated with sea lion colonies.

### Can I See the Iguana While Diving?

The land iguana is seen on shore during a permitted walk. Underwater at Santa Fe, visitors may encounter sea lions, fish, turtles and rays instead.

### How Long Is the Boat Trip to Santa Fe?

Ada Tours' diving program gives a guideline of around one hour from base. Confirm the crossing duration with the operator for your particular trip.

### Is Santa Fe Included on Every Ada Tours Galápagos Tour?

No. The [diving program](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-diving-4-5-days/) lists it as one possible site. The precise dives are selected before departure.

### Can I Visit Santa Fe Without a Diving Certificate?

A permitted land walk does not require diving certification. Scuba dives follow the individual dive center's conditions; any beginner program must be arranged separately.
